Lee et al. developed a GFP-based flow cytometry assay of RAG recombination activity and measured 79 RAG1 mutations in mouse Rag1-/- pro-B cells, reporting correlation between defective recombination activity of mutant hRAG1 and severity of clinical and immunologic phenotype, and that RAG1 mutants can induce specific abnormalities of the VDJ recombination process.

Notarangelo et al. review RAG mutations as producing biochemical defects in recombination activity of mutant RAG proteins, with crystal structure of the RAG complex used to interpret phenotypic diversity.

UniProtKB function of RAG1_HUMAN: Catalytic component of the RAG complex, a multiprotein complex that mediates the DNA cleavage phase during V(D)J recombination. V(D)J recombination assembles a diverse repertoire of immunoglobulin and T-cell receptor genes in developing B and T-lymphocytes through rearrangement of different V (variable), in some cases D (diversity), and J (joining) gene segments. In the RAG complex, RAG1 mediates the DNA-binding to …

Asai et al. report that RAG1 and RAG2 missense mutations in RAG-deficient patients were located in active core regions, and that V(D)J recombination activity of each mutant ranged from half of wild-type activity to none, with a significant decrease in average recombination activity in each patient.

UniProtKB subunit annotation: Homodimer. Component of the RAG complex composed of core components RAG1 and RAG2, and associated component HMGB1 or HMGB2. Interacts with DCAF1, leading to recruitment of the CUL4A-RBX1-DDB1-DCAF1/VPRBP complex to ubiquitinate proteins and limit error-prone repair during V(D)J recombination (By similarity)

Core RAG1 knock-in mice (RAG1 c/c) generate significant B and T cell numbers, showing that core RAG1 despite lacking noncore regions retains in vivo function, which indicates a role for noncore regions in RAG1 activity.
UniProtKB annotates residues 392-459 of P15918 as DNA binding: NBD; evidence: match to sequence model evidence used in manual assertion.

N-terminal RAG1 frameshift mutations in Omenn's syndrome lead to internal methionine usage and partial V(D)J recombination activity, which the authors use to reveal a fundamental role in vivo for the N-terminal domains of RAG1.
InterPro annotates residues 390-460 of P15918 as domain: RAG nonamer-binding domain; evidence: match to sequence model evidence used in automatic assertion.

payload.statement: Arg404 sits in the RAG1 nonamer-binding/DNA-binding region (residues 392-459). Its positive side chain likely contacts the RSS DNA phosphate backbone, and Arg-to-Gln removes that charge and the contact, which lowers DNA binding and so cleavage.
payload.would_refute: Any DNA-bound RAG1 model or structure in which no R404 side-chain atom lies within about 4 Å of DNA, and the R404Q model shows no change in predicted DNA-contact energy or interface geometry.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Ranked first because the residue lies in the annotated DNA-binding NBD (E10, E12) and the record links RAG1 missense variants to biochemical loss of recombination activity (E5, E7). Support is indirect: no source states that R404 contacts DNA (G2), and the charge-loss argument is my inference. Still missing: a DNA-bound structure or model placing R404 (G2, G4), and any mutant-specific recombination assay (G1, G5).

payload.statement: R404 is part of a buried or intra-domain salt bridge or hydrogen-bond network in the NBD fold. Replacing the Arg with Gln destabilises the folded domain, so the protein is misfolded or unstable and recombination fails.
payload.would_refute: A folding-stability calculation (for example FoldX or Rosetta ΔΔG) on the AlphaFold model gives |ΔΔG| below about 1 kcal/mol, or the R404 side chain is solvent-exposed with no intra-domain partner, and local pLDDT around residue 404 is low.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Ranked second. Conservation is maximal (E14) and several predictors call the substitution damaging (E13, E15, E16), but those scores do not separate folding from binding effects and none is residue-specific ΔΔG. The global mean pLDDT is 81.56 (E18), which gives no local evidence. Missing: per-residue pLDDT and side-chain burial at 404, and a ΔΔG calculation (G4).

payload.statement: R404 lies at a RAG1 self-association or RAG1-RAG2 interface, so its Arg side chain makes an inter-chain contact needed to assemble the active recombinase complex. The Gln substitution weakens that contact and blocks complex assembly.
payload.would_refute: In the RAG1 homodimer or RAG1-RAG2 complex model, the R404 side chain lies more than about 10 Å from any atom of the partner chain, and the R404Q substitution does not change predicted interface area or binding energy.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis

payload.description: FoldX predicted folding free-energy change (ddG) for R404Q on the AlphaFold model via EBI ProtVar, with local pLDDT at residue 404 and the ddG of other disease substitutions at the same residue. payload.expected_learning_reasoning: H2 is refuted if |ddG| is below about 1 kcal/mol with confident local pLDDT, and gains strongly if ddG is at or above the destabilising threshold. Either outcome moves H2 in opposite directions, and H2 is the only hypothesis this test can move, so the ranking changes. G5 (no functional assays at 404) means no other evidence currently tests H2. Limitation: FoldX errors are near 1 kcal/mol, so a neutral result weakens H2 without excluding it, and a neutral result does not confirm H1 or H3.

per_hypothesis.why: T1 measures folding stability, not DNA contact, so it does not bear on H1's nucleic-acid mechanism. R404Q gave FoldX ddG -0.79 kcal/mol, which is neutral for stability and says nothing about phosphate-backbone contact.

H2's pre-stated would_refute criterion was |ddG| below about 1 kcal/mol. T1 measured ddG -0.79 kcal/mol (E-result T1, FoldX on AF-P15918-F1), and residue 404 pLDDT is 93.56, so the model is confident there and the result is interpretable. The other clause (exposed side chain with low pLDDT) does not apply, but the first clause alone is met. Caveat: FoldX error is about 1 kcal/mol, so the refutation is of destabilisation large enough to be a clear loss, not a proof that no fold change occurs.
T1 is a stability test and does not measure any RAG1 self-association or RAG1-RAG2 interface. Interface geometry at R404 was not tested (T2 and T4 not run).

payload.uncertainty: T1 is a single computational FoldX prediction on one AlphaFold model, with about 1 kcal/mol error, so a -0.79 value is not a precise measurement. The control R404W also gave -0.79 kcal/mol, so the substitution-specific signal is absent, and the control is consistent with a neutral stability effect at this residue. A neutral ddG does not show the variant is tolerated: ClinVar Pathogenic (E1), AlphaMissense 0.953 (E13) and conservation 1.0 (E14) still need explaining by a non-folding mechanism. T2, T3 and T4 were not run, so H1 and H3 remain untested directly. No experimental validation exists for any of these predictions; all results here are computational predictions to be checked in the laboratory.

payload.why: Previous favourite was H1 and its strongest rival is H3 (H2 is now refuted by T1). H1 keeps direct residue-level support: the DNA-binding annotation for residues 392-459 (E10), the NBD match (E12), the literature that RAG mutants lose cleavage/recombination activity (E5, E7), and the high conservation (E14, 1.0) and AlphaMissense score (E13, 0.953) at R404. H3 has only general support: the homodimer and RAG1-RAG2 complex annotation (E8), and the mutant recombination assays (E4, E9), none of which names residue 404. T1 (ddG -0.79, pLDDT 93.56) removed the fold-destabilisation rival H2 but did not touch H1 or H3, so the ranking is unchanged. ## Question
Which molecular mechanism best explains the loss of function of RAG1 p.Arg404Gln (UniProt P15918), and does one targeted computational test change the starting conclusion? [E1, E6]

## Evidence
ClinVar classes NM_000448.3 c.1211G>A (p.Arg404Gln) as Pathogenic, reviewed by an expert panel [E1]. RAG1 is the catalytic component of the RAG complex that mediates DNA cleavage in V(D)J recombination [E6]. Residues 392-459 are annotated as DNA-binding (NBD) [E10, E12]. Literature reports reduced recombination activity for RAG mutants [E5, E7]. AlphaMissense gives 0.953 and conservation is 1.0 [E13, E14]. No experimental structure or functional assay covers residue 404 [E17, G4, G5], and no paper reports this substitution specifically [G1].

## Agent-generated hypotheses
- H1 (nucleic-acid binding, rank 1): the Arg side chain contacts RSS DNA [H1].
- H2 (stability/folding, rank 2): the Arg sits in an intra-domain network whose loss destabilises the fold [H2].
- H3 (protein interaction, rank 3): the Arg makes an inter-chain contact in RAG1 or RAG1-RAG2 assembly [H3].

## Tests considered and the choice
H1 was favoured before the test [H1]. Four tests were considered: T1 stability (expected learning 0.7, feasibility 0.8, no approval), T2 structural context (0.3), T3 ligand contact (feasibility 0), and T4 structure comparison (120 compute s, approval needed, feasibility 0.1) [T1, T2, T3, T4]. T1 was chosen for its highest expected learning and no approval need. The first plan was blocked only by a refused note; the re-submitted plan was cleared [T1].

## Result
FoldX predicts a ddG of -0.79 kcal/mol for R404Q on the AlphaFold model, below the 2.0 kcal/mol destabilising threshold, with residue pLDDT 93.56 [T1, E20, E21]. The R404W substitution gives the same value [E22].

## Updated decision
H1 is still favoured after the test [H1]. H2 is refuted by the T1 result [H2, T1]. H3 is unchanged [H3]. The decision did not change. No reopening applied, because the test completed and the favoured hypothesis was not weakened [H1].

## Uncertainty and validation still needed
These are computational predictions, and none has been validated experimentally [T1]. T1 is a single FoldX prediction on one AlphaFold model [T1]. A neutral ddG does not explain the Pathogenic classification, so a non-folding mechanism is still needed [E1, T1]. H1 and H3 remain untested directly, because T2 and T4 were not run [T2, T4].

## Next experiment
A computational DNA-contact check on an experimental RAG1 structure with bound RSS DNA, measuring the distance from R404 atoms to DNA [H1]. This is the would-refute test for H1 [H1]. A laboratory EMSA comparing RAG1 wild-type and R404Q binding to an RSS is the follow-up [H1].
